title: Why use Redis
context: Why would you use Redis in a backend?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Redis questions (1 of 2)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Redis is an in-memory data store with rich types, so it serves as a cache, a session store, a rate limiter, a queue, a leaderboard or a lock service. It is shared by all application instances, unlike a process-local cache. It has persistence options and replication, so it can survive restarts. Typical use is to reduce load on a slower database, and to share fast state between servers.

points.title: Shared fast state
points.why: Several app servers can read and write the same Redis data quickly.

points.title: Rich data types
points.why: Lists, sets, sorted sets and hashes solve common problems without custom code.
